key_insight: Grain-boundary segregation in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni slows the onset of plastic flow, mainly by reducing the early plastic strain rate.
engineering_relevance: Tuning grain-boundary chemistry could improve short-term load-bearing resistance in nanocrystalline austenitic steels without changing dislocation content.
method: Hybrid molecular dynamics/Monte Carlo simulations on three independent nanocrystalline polycrystals
Compared segregated, annealed, and random controls on the same microstructures
Tested constant-stress creep and fixed-strain-rate loading across 300, 750, and 950 K
evidence_signal: Under 4.6 GPa at 300 K, segregated polycrystals reached 50% strain about 16% later than random controls, and showed a 6-7% higher peak stress at fixed strain rate across all tested temperatures.
watch_item: The measured Cr enrichment depends strongly on the chosen reference region, so composition conclusions should be interpreted carefully.
paper_title: Grain-boundary segregation delays the onset of plastic flow in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni
